OLID uses a hierarchical annotation model split into three levels to distinguish whether language is offensive (A), and the type (B) and target (C) of the offensive language. [2]

questions.question: How are the different components of the model trained? Is it trained end-to-end?

result.answer:
The proposed BERT-based natural language generation model can be trained end-to-end without handcrafted features. [1]
BERT is used on both the encoder and decoder of a seq2seq model, with a two-stage decoding structure. [2]
During training, the model's objective is the sum of the two processes, jointly trained using the teacher-forcing algorithm. [3]
During training, the ground-truth summary is fed to each decoder and the objective is minimized. [3]
The model loss is defined as the sum of the decoder loss and the refine loss. [4]
All models in this work are built on BERT_BASE. [5]

The paper discusses the state of the art on conversational systems from three perspectives: types of interactions, types of architecture, and types of context reasoning, then presents a table consolidating and comparing them. [1]
The paper states that the state of the art for creating chatbots that can participate in multiparty conversations is currently a combination of research on chatbot creation and research on coordination or governance of multi-agent systems. [2]
The paper states it is not meant to advance the state of the art on the norms for MPCS. [3]
The authors say they did not explicitly define the norms because the goal was to evaluate the overall architecture, not to enhance the state of the art on norms specification for conversational systems. [4]
